neighbours.label: The recipient pronoun right after give/giving when a person is given attention or treatment (give her a compliment, gave me a hard time, give him water)
fire: At the party, my aunt walked over to give me a big hug.
The coach refused to give him another chance after the game.
When the baby cried, the nurse came to give her a bottle.
Every morning the neighbors give us a friendly wave.
My teacher would always give me extra homework on Fridays.
If you see the guard, give him my thanks.
The judges decided to give them a second round.
Strangers kept giving her advice about the stroller.
quiet: At the party, my aunt walked over to hug me tightly.
The coach refused to let the team play another game.
When the baby cried, the nurse came to warm a bottle.
Every morning the neighbors wave from across the street.
My teacher would always assign extra homework on Fridays.
If you see the guard, thank him for me.
The judges decided to schedule a second round.
Strangers kept looking at the stroller on the bus.

predictions: ' me/him/her/them' after give/gave/giving reach 0.3-0.6; the same scenes with another verb, or give + a thing to an inanimate place, stay under 0.2.
notes: Probe: 'give him some water' 0.565 vs 'bring some water' 0.231; 'give me compliments' 0.477 vs 'stop me' 0.067; 'giving me a hard time' 0.324; 'give the form to the front desk' 0.124. Also 'lots of praise' 0.466 and 'unwelcome physical contact' 0.465, not covered.
